President Trump and Chinese leader Xi Jinping wrapped up a state visit today. NPR's Emily
Fang reports they traded praise for each other but didn't address fundamental issues.
While showing Xi around the National Archives, Trump told reporters,
"Meetings with Xi went great." Trump also posted on social media that he will be heading to the
Chinese city of Shenzhen in November to meet Xi again, and that Xi will come back to the U.S.

over competition in artificial intelligence and semiconductors and rare-earth minerals.
Nevertheless, at a state dinner this week, both Trump and Xi were all smiles and toasted each other.
Emily Fang, NPR News. The Supreme Court has revived for now a federal data system. The
Department of Homeland Security revamped into a tool to check the citizenship of millions of
Americans on voter rolls. The tool has mistakenly flagged some eligible voters as potential non-citizens.
NPR's Jude Joffe-Bloch has more on the Systematic Alien Verification for Entitlements, or SAVE, program.
SAVE's the Department of Homeland Security data system. It's been around for 40 years.
It was created so government agencies could check non-citizens' immigration status.
And it used to be exclusively foreign-born people who were in this data system.
But last year, the Trump administration did a huge overhaul and linked it to social security
data so most American citizenship could be checked. It also made changes so states could
do bulk queries and upload their entire voter rolls to find non-citizens or deceased individuals.
NPR's Jude Joffe-Bloch reporting. An appeals court heard arguments today on whether to bring
back to the U.S. more than 100 people deported to Venezuela last year. NPR's Nate Perez reports.
The Venezuelans were deported under the Alien Enemies Act, a rarely used policy previously
reserved for wartime. They were sent to El Salvador's infamous prison, Secort,
despite a court ordering the return of their flight. Lawyers for the deported men said the
U.S. government violated their due process rights as most of the plaintiffs were in immigration
proceedings prior to being detained. But some on the three-judge panel were skeptical whether
this appeals court is capable of determining whether the deported men could challenge their
imprisonment in a foreign country. The case could be decided by next week. Nate Perez, NPR News.
From Washington, you're listening to NPR News.

Mikey Sherrill gave Lieutenant Governor Dale Caldwell an ultimatum that he resigned by the

from the festivities. Locals and tourists alike are celebrating with fireworks, pink outfits,

Garth Brooks Honky Tonk, Friends in Low Places, is serving up a cocktail called Cup of Ambition

And live music venues across the city closed out the workday by playing
Parton's iconic workers anthem. For NPR News, I'm Mariana Bacchiao in Nashville.

Leo called for reflection on life's dignity, urging AI developers to prioritize the common good.
